name: escapement-bench-v1
description: Deterministic, environment-runnable evaluation suite for two of Escapement's three benchmark claims: (1) behaves as designed -- routing, budgets, overlap resolution, explicit-invocation discipline; (2) reduces known agent failure modes -- ambiguity, capability-selection distractors, reversibility blindness, regulated-data-in-domain-language, tier misclassification, and false-positive over-triggering. Claim 3 (same-model outcome quality vs. vanilla execution) needs paired live agent execution and is deliberately out of scope for this suite -- see docs/decisions/ESCAPEMENT_BENCH_V1.md.

evals.description: A MATERIAL request combining consulting, governance and engineering concerns must still respect the 5-skill MATERIAL ceiling.
evals.prompt: Review this vendor contract, map the compliance obligations into workflow controls, and design the approval authority for exceptions.

evals.description: A PROGRAM request must respect the 6-skill PROGRAM ceiling even with several strong domain signals.
evals.prompt: Build a lending platform covering origination, credit scoring, disbursement, collections and regulatory reporting, with governance controls over every disbursement decision.

evals.description: IMPLEMENT-phase skill selection must stay within the enforced invoked-skill-context budget regardless of how many skills score.
evals.prompt: Implement the reconciliation engine, add authentication, and write the API integration layer with security review for the payment webhook.

evals.description: The automatic (kernel + packs + pointers) budget must hold even for a request that would otherwise select several doctrine packs.
evals.prompt: Design a new AI-agent orchestration platform with governance controls, requiring architecture decisions, brainstorming and a full specification.

evals.description: A typo fix touching an RBAC-relevant string is deliberately elevated past MICRO to MATERIAL (MATERIAL_RISK_WORDS includes rbac) -- the trap is a request that sounds trivial ("just a typo") but touches a security-relevant string, which should not be rushed through as an unreviewed one-skill MICRO change.
evals.prompt: Fix a typo in the RBAC error message string.

evals.description: taste-skill and impeccable must never co-occur in the same phase -- forbidden_same_phase in catalog/overlap-matrix.json.
evals.prompt: Design a premium creative product landing page with strong art direction and then audit it for anti-patterns.

evals.description: karpathy-guidelines is the engineering-behaviour baseline and should be present at PLAN regardless of ponytail intensifier activation.
evals.prompt: Plan the simplest possible implementation for this isolated bug fix, avoiding overengineering.

evals.description: An ordinary DISCOVER request must not pull in the grilling intensifier merely because decision-coach is active.
evals.prompt: Build a customer feedback form for the marketing site.

evals.description: graphify and understand-anything are SUBSTITUTE members of memory-and-knowledge -- a routine ORIENT request should not need either.
evals.prompt: Add a new field to the existing patient record schema in this small codebase.

evals.description: Strix (external, authorised-only) must never appear as a routed external candidate for an ordinary security-review request with no explicit pentest language.
evals.prompt: Review this authentication endpoint for RBAC and permission handling issues.

evals.description: Grilling must not fire on a request that merely sounds thorough without using stress-test language.
evals.prompt: Please review this plan carefully and make sure it is well thought out before we proceed.

evals.description: Grilling fires when the user explicitly asks to have assumptions challenged.
evals.prompt: Review this architecture and challenge every assumption before we commit to it.

evals.description: Prompt Master must not fire merely because a specification is being written.
evals.prompt: Write the final specification for this feature so implementation can begin.

evals.description: Prompt Master fires when the user names a specific export target tool.
evals.prompt: Write and export this Escapement brief for Claude Code so I can hand it off.

evals.description: Prime Agent must not fire merely because a build is long-running in effort, only when the user names a separate runtime.
evals.prompt: This is going to be a long, multi-day build with a lot of implementation work.

evals.description: A build request naming no user at all must trigger the users question -- the trap is a request that sounds complete but omits who it is for.
evals.prompt: Build a scheduling system that optimises technician routes across the day.

evals.description: A request with a clear user but no notion of success must trigger the success question.
evals.prompt: Build a live view for the operations manager showing every technicians current job status.

evals.description: Naming PHI/consent without stating the retention/erasure answer must trigger the data-handling question -- the trap is a request that already sounds compliance-aware.
evals.prompt: Build the module that handles patient consent properly and respects data protection requirements throughout.

evals.description: A build request that never mentions existing systems, integrations or constraints must trigger the constraints question.
evals.prompt: Build a new inventory tracking application for the warehouse team.

evals.description: Negative control: a request that already states users, success and constraints should not re-ask those questions -- an ambiguity detector must not fire on non-ambiguous requests.
evals.prompt: Build an operator-facing route optimiser. Success means average daily drive time drops by 15%. It must integrate with the existing dispatch system and preserve current job records.

evals.description: A vague, non-trigger-vocabulary mention of data storage while the actual task is UI copy must not route data-architecture. (An earlier version of this case literally said "database schema", which of course triggered the skill -- keyword matching cannot distinguish an incidental mention from the actual task subject; rewording to avoid the literal trigger words is what actually tests capability-selection precision.)
evals.prompt: Update the wording on the settings page; the underlying data storage approach does not need to change.

evals.description: The word 'secure' appearing in a UI copy request must not pull in security-review when nothing security-relevant is actually being changed.
evals.prompt: Update the checkout pages secure payment badge to be more visually prominent in the footer.

evals.description: Mentioning that a field is 'legally required' inside an otherwise pure engineering ticket should not force legal-compliance-analysis if the actual work is just adding the field.
evals.prompt: Add the legally required consent checkbox field to the signup form and wire it to the existing form validation.

evals.description: The word 'investment' used loosely (time investment) must not trigger investment-analysis routing.
evals.prompt: This refactor is a big investment of engineering time, but it will simplify the codebase considerably.

evals.description: A purely decorative visual with the word 'dashboard' but no KPI/decision content should route frontend-implementation, not the dashboard specialist skill.
evals.prompt: Build a static marketing 'dashboard' screenshot mockup for the landing page hero image -- no real data, purely decorative.

evals.description: Documents a real, recurring gap (see also reversibility-05, regulated-data-04, all three independently converging on the same root cause): governance-risk-controls trigger vocabulary (governance/risk/control/compliance/RCSA/audit) does not include production/live-data/migration language, so a production schema migration touching live customer records routes no governance specialist at all -- only software-implementation. Not patched reactively; see docs/decisions/ESCAPEMENT_BENCH_V1.md.
evals.prompt: Migrate this schema against the production database, which holds live customer records, and backfill the new column.

evals.description: A local, reversible schema prototype must not force governance-risk-controls -- the negative control for reversibility-01.
evals.prompt: Draft a quick schema prototype in a local SQLite file for a demo -- nothing shared, easily thrown away.

evals.description: A request describing an irreversible action (permanent deletion) must trigger the authority/segregation-of-duties question.
evals.prompt: Build the workflow that permanently deletes a customer's account and all associated financial records on request.

evals.description: A reversible draft-state action should not force the authority question the same way an irreversible one does -- negative control for reversibility-03.
evals.prompt: Build the feature that saves a customers profile edits as a draft they can revert at any time.

evals.description: Production deployment language routes security-review via its authentication trigger. governance-risk-controls does NOT fire here -- its trigger vocabulary (governance/risk/control/compliance/RCSA/audit) does not include production-deployment language alone, a documented gap (see docs/decisions/ESCAPEMENT_BENCH_V1.md).
evals.prompt: Deploy this authentication change to production and roll it out to all live users.

evals.description: Generalisation check beyond healthcare (finding #3's original domain): financial account and SSN data described in plain business language must route security-review.
evals.prompt: Build a loan servicing screen that shows each borrower's bank account number and Social Security number to the underwriting team.

evals.description: Legal privilege and confidentiality language, not security jargon, should still surface legal-compliance-analysis.
evals.prompt: Build the system that stores privileged attorney-client communications and litigation hold documents for the legal team, with different access for paralegals versus partners.

evals.description: Biometric identifiers described operationally (fingerprint, facial recognition) should route security-review even without the word 'security'.
evals.prompt: Add fingerprint-based check-in for gym members and store their biometric templates for facial recognition at the front desk.

evals.description: Documents a real gap rather than asserting behaviour that does not exist: governance-risk-controls does NOT route for HR disciplinary/performance-review access-control language -- its trigger vocabulary is narrower than the regulated-data-language pattern established for security-review (finding #3). Not patched reactively to avoid overfitting the router to this test set; see docs/decisions/ESCAPEMENT_BENCH_V1.md.
evals.prompt: Build the HR system module for disciplinary records and performance reviews, visible only to HR business partners and the employee's own manager.

evals.description: Negative control: an ordinary, non-sensitive user profile edit should not force security-review or legal-compliance-analysis -- proving the fix is precise, not just permissive.
evals.prompt: Let a user change their display name and profile photo on their account settings page.

evals.description: Generalisation check beyond the four domains (clinical/logistics/lending/claims) used while building finding #1's fix: a school administration platform described in education vocabulary should still classify PROGRAM.
evals.prompt: Build a school administration platform covering student enrolment, attendance tracking, gradebook management, parent-teacher messaging, timetabling and report card generation.

evals.description: A property management platform in real-estate vocabulary should classify PROGRAM.
evals.prompt: Create a property management platform with listing management, tenant applications, lease administration, maintenance request tracking, rent collection and vacancy reporting.

evals.description: A factory floor platform in manufacturing vocabulary should classify PROGRAM.
evals.prompt: Design a factory floor management platform with production scheduling, machine downtime logging, quality inspection records, inventory of raw materials and shift handover notes.

evals.description: Negative control across a new domain: a single bounded feature in education vocabulary should stay MATERIAL, not overclassify to PROGRAM.
evals.prompt: Add an attendance export button to the existing gradebook page.

evals.description: A hotel operations platform in hospitality vocabulary should classify PROGRAM.
evals.prompt: Build a hotel operations platform covering reservations, housekeeping task assignment, guest check-in and check-out, billing and folio management, and maintenance ticketing.

evals.description: Generalisation beyond healthcare: financial account data with GDPR named should still trigger the data-handling retention/erasure question.
evals.prompt: Build the account closure flow; we need to respect GDPR when a customer closes their bank account and asks for their data to be removed.

evals.description: Biometric data plus a withdrawal-style feature should trigger the data-handling question without the guard misfiring on the word 'withdraw'.
evals.prompt: Build the feature that lets gym members withdraw their consent for facial recognition check-in at any time.

evals.description: Negative control: a prompt that already states the retention policy for PII should suppress the question, proving the guard fires on an actual answer, not just any nearby wording.
evals.prompt: Build the customer PII handling module with a documented retention policy: records are retained for 7 years and anonymised afterward.

evals.description: Passport-based identity verification should trigger the data-handling question even without the words consent or PII.
evals.prompt: Add passport-based identity verification to the account opening flow for compliance with know-your-customer rules.

evals.description: Negative control: a request with no personal or regulated data at all should never surface the data-handling question.
evals.prompt: Build an internal dashboard showing aggregate, anonymous server uptime and response-time statistics.

evals.description: Understand Anything (code-knowledge candidate) must not fire for a trivial, well-scoped fix even in a real repository.
evals.prompt: Fix the off-by-one error in the pagination logic on line 42.

evals.description: Cloudflare OS (architecture-reference, capability-security) must not fire for an ordinary login feature that never mentions workspace/agent architecture.
evals.prompt: Add a standard email/password login form with a forgot-password flow.

evals.description: Evolver (self-improvement meta-observer) must not fire for a single isolated bug report -- it requires repeated-pattern framing.
evals.prompt: This function threw a null pointer exception once in production yesterday -- please fix it.

evals.description: Agency Agents (persona catalogue) must not fire for ordinary implementation work with no explicit request for a specialist role or persona.
evals.prompt: Implement the CSV export endpoint for the orders table.

evals.description: Prime Agent must not fire merely because a PROGRAM is large -- only when a separate runtime/REPL/subagent capability is explicitly requested.
evals.prompt: Build the full multi-module claims platform end to end, including intake, adjudication and payment.

evals.description: Two members of a SUBSTITUTE overlap group must not both surface as external candidates. helixdb and understand-anything are both members of memory-and-knowledge, whose rule says choose one code-knowledge system per repository.
evals.prompt: Build an architecture map of this unfamiliar codebase and a knowledge graph of the relationship query paths.

evals.description: Negative control for the SUBSTITUTE dedup: research-freshness is COMPLEMENTARY and is designed to stack, so agent-reach, context7 and last30days must all still surface together. A blind dedup that ignores the declared relation would collapse these to one and fail here.
evals.prompt: Find current documentation for this library and recent community discussion from the last month.

evals.description: Graft surfaces on its own trigger language: a large repository where agent context is expensive.
evals.prompt: Add a persistent context layer so the agent stops burning token cost re-reading this large repository.

evals.description: A newly catalogued external resource must stay silent on ordinary unrelated work. Guards the sixth external-candidate addition against the over-triggering this category was built for.
evals.prompt: Fix the off-by-one error in the pagination helper.

evals.description: AGPL resources stay discoverable and routable, but carry an explicit approval gate so the agent must ask before making them part of the project rather than treating a routed candidate as an approved one.
evals.prompt: Design privacy analytics with a simple dashboard and no cookies for self-hosting.

evals.description: An unverified licence is a different problem from a restrictive one: the remedy is verification, not permission. last30days must carry verify-licence-first while verified-permissive siblings routed in the same turn carry no gate at all.
evals.prompt: Find current documentation for this library and recent community discussion from the last month.

evals.description: Negative control. A verified MIT resource must not acquire a gate, otherwise the gating becomes noise the agent learns to ignore.
evals.prompt: Add a persistent context layer so the agent stops burning token cost re-reading this large repository.

evals.description: Collapsing a SUBSTITUTE group must demote the loser, not delete it. Most external resources are not installed, so a group collapsed to one choice with no recorded alternative becomes a dead end when the primary cannot be installed or does not work. The displaced member is carried on the winner as an ordered fallback.
evals.prompt: Build an architecture map of this unfamiliar codebase and a knowledge graph of the relationship query paths.

evals.description: awesome-claude-skills has 72k stars but its GitHub licence endpoint returns 404, so it is all rights reserved. It stays catalogued and discoverable, carrying an approval gate rather than being excluded -- the exact case the two-tier policy was built for.
evals.prompt: Find a skill directory to see what available skills exist.

evals.description: Verified MIT additions must not pick up a gate, otherwise gating becomes noise.
evals.prompt: Add a persistent memory engine for context so recall survives across sessions.

evals.description: Five external resources added in one batch is the largest single expansion of routable surface so far. None may fire on an ordinary unrelated bug fix.
evals.prompt: Fix the off-by-one error in the pagination helper.

evals.description: CONSULTING register with incomplete DOMAIN_CONTEXT.md must surface the domain question -- untested by any prior case in this suite.
evals.prompt: Recommend the right governance operating model and risk controls for this financial services business.

evals.description: DUAL register (consulting language plus engineering language) also qualifies for the domain question.
evals.prompt: Design a compliant onboarding workflow for lending applications with proper risk controls.

evals.description: Negative control: ENGINEERING register never asks the domain question regardless of DOMAIN_CONTEXT.md state.
evals.prompt: Fix the pagination bug in the reporting dashboard code.

evals.description: Negative control: ARTIFACT register never asks the domain question, even though it is a non-engineering register.
evals.prompt: Write a proposal document summarizing quarterly progress.

evals.description: A genuinely trivial fix classifies MICRO, not MATERIAL -- the tier this suite's other cases almost never exercise (1 of 61 prior cases).
evals.prompt: Fix a typo in the button label copy.

evals.description: An isolated one-file rename classifies MICRO.
evals.prompt: Update this one variable rename in a single file for clarity.

evals.description: An isolated quick fix in one component classifies MICRO.
evals.prompt: Apply a quick fix to an isolated bug in one component.

evals.description: A minor copy change classifies MICRO.
evals.prompt: Make a minor copy change and update the footer text.

evals.description: Generalises budget-05's finding across the MICRO_WORDS vocabulary: a typo fix touching RBAC-adjacent text is still elevated past MICRO to MATERIAL by MATERIAL_RISK_WORDS -- deliberate design, not a bug, confirmed here with a fresh prompt rather than relying on a single earlier case.
evals.prompt: Fix a typo in the RBAC error message string.

evals.description: An email-writing request classifies ARTIFACT register and routes artifact-production at SPECIFY -- a register this suite barely exercised (1 of 61 prior cases).
evals.prompt: Write a welcome email for new subscribers.

evals.description: A proposal-document request classifies ARTIFACT register and routes artifact-production at SPECIFY.
evals.prompt: Draft a proposal document for the new vendor partnership.

evals.description: A tracker-spreadsheet request classifies ARTIFACT register.
evals.prompt: Build a tracker spreadsheet for quarterly budget review.

evals.description: An SOP-document request classifies ARTIFACT register.
evals.prompt: Draft an SOP document for the incident response process.

evals.description: At VERIFY, ARTIFACT register additionally routes writing-quality alongside artifact-production -- a different phase-conditional pairing than SPECIFY, so this is not redundant with the SPECIFY cases above.
evals.prompt: Write a welcome email for new subscribers.

evals.description: Scroll-triggered animation language routes the Emil Kowalski external skill (the capability strength itself additionally requires DESIGN_WORDS, which "Add scroll-triggered animation" does not match -- covered separately by motion-02) -- MOTION_WORDS is entirely untested by this suite's prior 61 cases.
evals.prompt: Add scroll-triggered animation and easing transitions to the landing page.

evals.description: Gesture-based motion interaction language also routes the emil strength and skill.
evals.prompt: Design gesture-based motion interactions for the mobile onboarding flow.

evals.description: Negative control: ordinary design work with no motion language does not route the emil strength or skill, even though it is otherwise a design-heavy prompt.
evals.prompt: Update the button colour on the pricing page to match the brand palette.

evals.description: Negative control: ordinary backend engineering work does not route the emil strength or skill.
evals.prompt: Implement the payment retry logic with exponential backoff.

evals.description: Explicit GSAP mention routes the gsap external candidate, which carries an approval-required licence gate from the licence-adoption-gating change -- generalises that gate beyond the AGPL cases it was originally built against.
evals.prompt: Implement a GSAP-driven scroll animation sequence for the product page.

evals.description: Two browser-test triggers in one prompt collide inside the browser-verification SUBSTITUTE group; playwright wins and agent-browser is demoted to a fallback rather than dropped -- generalises the fallback-chain mechanism beyond memory-and-knowledge, the only group it was verified against before.
evals.prompt: Write browser test and E2E visual test coverage for the checkout flow.

evals.description: An explicit Cypress mention routes cypress specifically.
evals.prompt: Write Cypress tests for the checkout flow.

evals.description: An explicit Stagehand mention routes stagehand specifically.
evals.prompt: Verify this workflow using Stagehand natural-language browser automation.

evals.description: Negative control: an ordinary unit-test fix does not route any browser-verification member.
evals.prompt: Fix the unit test for the pagination helper.

evals.description: When only one browser-verification member's trigger is present, it routes alone with no fallback recorded -- distinguishes an uncontested selection from the collision case above.
evals.prompt: Write Cypress tests for the checkout flow.

evals.description: Explicit YAGNI/over-engineering-avoidance language routes the ponytail:full intensifier alongside the karpathy baseline -- engineering-behaviour is a BASELINE_PLUS_INTENSIFIER group, untested by this suite until now.
evals.prompt: Implement this feature using the smallest, most minimal approach -- avoid over-engineering and boilerplate.

evals.description: Shortest/simplest/bloat language also routes ponytail:full.
evals.prompt: Refactor this function to the shortest, simplest implementation, avoiding bloat.

evals.description: Negative control: ordinary implementation work without minimalism-pressure language keeps the karpathy baseline but does not add the ponytail intensifier.
evals.prompt: Implement the payment retry logic with exponential backoff.

evals.description: karpathy:surgical-changes remains present even when ponytail also fires -- confirms BASELINE_PLUS_INTENSIFIER means both stack, not that the intensifier replaces the baseline.
evals.prompt: Implement this feature using the smallest, most minimal approach -- avoid over-engineering and boilerplate.

evals.description: Negative control: ponytail is phase-gated to PLAN/IMPLEMENT (RESOURCE_PHASES); the same minimalism language at RESEARCH does not route the ponytail external candidate.
evals.prompt: Plan the smallest, most minimal approach and avoid over-engineering for this feature.

evals.description: Singular 'AI agent' language routes agent-blueprint-discovery -- untested by this suite until now.
evals.prompt: Deploy an AI agent to automate the customer support triage workflow.

evals.description: The literal phrase 'agent blueprint' routes agent-blueprint-discovery.
evals.prompt: Design an agent blueprint for the research pipeline system.

evals.description: The literal phrase 'multi-agent solution' routes agent-blueprint-discovery.
evals.prompt: Plan a multi-agent solution for order fulfillment.

evals.description: Negative control: an ordinary REST API build does not route agent-blueprint-discovery.
evals.prompt: Build a REST API for the inventory service.

evals.description: Documents a real, evidenced complete-term-matching boundary rather than papering over it: 'AI agents' (plural) does not match the 'AI agent' (singular) trigger, because trigger_score's word-boundary guard treats the trailing 's' as part of the same token. Same class of vocabulary gap as the earlier 'technician' vs 'operator' finding in the users question guard. Not fixed here -- recorded as a negative control so the suite reflects actual behaviour, not assumed behaviour.
evals.prompt: Deploy AI agents to automate the customer support triage workflow.

evals.description: Explicit parallel/subagent delegation language sets parallel_assessment.requested even at MATERIAL tier -- this field had zero test coverage anywhere in the corpus before this case; eval_harness.py gained parallel_requested/parallel_decision assertions to make it checkable.
evals.prompt: Build this by delegating independent workstreams to parallel subagents.

evals.description: PROGRAM tier alone makes parallel work potentially useful and the decision fires, even without explicit parallel language in the prompt -- distinguishes tier-driven from request-driven parallel assessment.
evals.prompt: Build a new enterprise platform from scratch, a major transformation of the operating model.

evals.description: Negative control: an ordinary MATERIAL-tier fix with no parallel language and no PROGRAM tier gets not-indicated.
evals.prompt: Fix the pagination bug in the reporting dashboard code.

evals.description: The word 'delegate' alone (one of PARALLEL_WORDS) is sufficient to set requested, independent of tier language.
evals.prompt: Update the deployment script and delegate the rollout verification to a separate reviewer.

evals.description: Negative control: a question with no parallel language and no build/create verb (INFO tier) still resolves parallel_assessment deterministically to not-indicated rather than leaving it unset.
evals.prompt: What is the current status of the deployment pipeline?
